title: DEF CON and the Origin of Security Capture-the-Flag Competitions (1996)
explainer: The first widely recognized computer-security CTF was held at DEF CON in 1996, starting as a handful of shared vulnerable services that contestants raced to exploit while judges tracked points. Over the following decades it grew into the qualifier-then-finals, attack/defense format used by today's elite competitions, including DARPA's autonomous Cyber Grand Challenge round in 2016. Advanced CTF play and original research sit inside a three-decade-old tradition of treating offensive security as a measurable, competitive skill rather than a purely defensive afterthought.
